// what this is: The guard's configuration for the synthetic lab workload — the stand-in for a client's application.
Nothing here is recognised by name: the guard knows MetricIndex.LatencyP95Ms, the cluster exports
labapp_request_duration_seconds, and this file is the only thing that connects them. That is the point.
CpuThrottleRatio comes from cadvisor rather than the app, and is unbound here because no pod carries
a CPU limit. OomEventsRate comes from kube-state-metrics; see its own comment for why not cadvisor.
app's own error counter over its request counter, which the map cannot express as a single source, so it
is left out and reported blind.

OomEventsRate.query: sum by (pod) (increase(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total{%selector%}[2m]) * on (namespace, pod, container) group_left() kube_pod_container_status_last_terminated_reason{%selector%,reason="OOMKilled"}) or sum by (pod) (increase(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total{%selector%}[2m]) * 0)
_comment: NOT container_oom_events_total. Measured 2026-08-08 against a pod Kubernetes reported as OOMKilled
with exit 137: that series read 0 for the killed pod, and across 43 series cluster-wide over an hour
the only distinct value present was 0.0 - cAdvisor does not populate it on this runtime. The channel
bound, reported a number, satisfied every coverage check and could never fire.
kube-state-metrics carries the fact in two series: the restart increase says an event happened inside
the window, the last-terminated reason says it was an OOM. A name and a kind cannot express a join,
which is why 'query' exists. Verbatim queries carry their own range - keep [2m] in step with
prometheus rate window by hand.
Bound 2026-08-09. It was absent from the metrics block, so the guard issued no query and counted
the channel blind in every cycle — 1 of 1, unchanged for the whole run.
The series only exist because the workload now carries a CPU limit: CFS accounting is created by a
quota, so without one there is nothing to read and no amount of binding would help.
1000m, not 200m, because SustainedThresholdOptions.ForCpuThrottling was calibrated on a pod limited
to one core, and a threshold describes the regime it was measured in.
Measured healthy at 1000m: per-pod share of a 20-minute window at or above the 5% threshold is
14.6-19.0%, against the rule's 25% - so the healthy population is quiet with margin on both sides.
ActiveRequests closes the hung-request gap: a request only enters the duration histogram when it
FINISHES, so while one hangs every latency percentile stays quiet. Measured 2026-08-09 with five
requests deliberately hung: labapp_active_requests read 6 while the histogram count read 0.
The exporter subtracts the scrape itself, so 0 means idle. Before that subtraction every pod
reported a flat 1.0 and the observer dominated the signal.
Floors from measurement: at rest 0 on all twelve pods, ten-minute maxima 0/1/2.
Closes a gap every current channel is structurally blind to: contention produces a latency cliff
with NORMAL CPU and NORMAL GC, because a thread waiting on a monitor is not running.
Measured 2026-08-09 with the contended lock ON THE REQUEST PATH: p50 47 -> 1210 ms, p95 63 -> 5837 ms,
throughput 759 -> 26 requests per 10 s, contention rate 2 -> 12/s. Clearing the fault returned every
number to its starting value.
The instrument is OBSERVABLE, so it reports nothing until polled - before RecordObservableInstruments
was called it read a clean, well-formed, permanent zero through sixteen contending threads.
Floor RECALIBRATED 2026-08-09. The first value, 0.064, came from a peak of 0.0514 measured over only
~3 minutes on pods that had just started, and it produced a false positive on an unfaulted pod within
the hour. Re-measured over a settled 20-minute window across both pod generations: healthy per-pod peak
0.0952/s, so healthy replicas routinely exceeded the old floor. 0.0952 x 1.25 = 0.119, which is still
about 97x below the injected fault at 11.6/s.
The lesson is the window, not the number: a floor calibrated on three minutes of a freshly rolled
population describes the rollout, not the workload.
First-chance exceptions. Distinct from ErrorRate, which counts 5xx RESPONSES: an exception that is
caught and retried never becomes a 5xx, so the error rate stays flat while the process is already
failing.
Measured 2026-08-09 with half of requests throwing-and-catching: exceptions 0 -> 40/s while the 5xx
rate stayed at 0, p95 went 63.2 -> 63.1 -> 63.2 ms, throughput was unchanged and NOT ONE response
was other than 200. This is the one of the three runtime channels where every existing channel is
genuinely blind - unlike lock contention, where CPU also moved.
Healthy is exactly 0 on all twelve pods, so InertChannels() will report it as constant-zero and
AMBIGUOUS. That is correct: it is what a working rare-event channel looks like when the rare event
has not happened.
